title: An equivariant homogeneous projective envelope
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $V\to S$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] admitting a locally closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_S$ for some $n\geq0$, where locally closed means a closed immersion into an open subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Let a finite group $H$ act on $V$ by $S$-automorphisms. There are an integer $N\geq0$, a homogeneous ideal $I\subset R[z_0,\ldots,z_N]$ with $\deg z_i=1$, and an action of $H$ on the graded $R$-algebra $A=R[z_0,\ldots,z_N]/I$ by graded $R$-algebra automorphisms, together with an $H$-equivariant open immersion $V\hookrightarrow M=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj]. The scheme $M$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^N_S$ [def-kun-projective]. The ring map $R\to A_0$ is surjective. The construction allows $V$ and $M$ to be empty and does not assume that $H$ acts faithfully or that its order is invertible in $R$.

source.place: Tag 01WD (lemma-segre-embedding), Tag 03GL (lemma-closed-in-projective-space), and morphisms.tex Tag 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image). Combine the product of all translates of the initial immersion, its equivariant Segre map, and scheme-theoretic closure. This combined equivariant assertion is an agent formulation of the homogeneous construction underlying Rydh Proposition 4.7.

proof.text: First verify quasi-compactness. By [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ has Noetherian underlying space. Such a space is quasi-compact: the ascending-chain condition on opens implies that the finite unions from any open cover have a maximal member, which must be the whole space. The one affine chart of $S$ makes it locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Thus $S$ is a Noetherian scheme, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $V$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], every open of $V$ is quasi-compact. Consequently every morphism from $V$ is quasi-compact, since inverse images of affine opens are opens of $V$.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian, and the cited Noetherian-space statements; preliminary check for the use of scheme-theoretic closure

proof.text: Fix the given immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^n_S$ and put $X=\prod_{g\in H}P$. Define $J_g=j\circ g^{-1}$ and $J=(J_g)_g:V\to X$. This is an immersion, as follows. The group is nonempty; separate the identity factor and write $X=P\times_S Y$, where $Y$ is the product of the remaining factors, or $S$ if there are none. Iterating [lem-chow-segre] exhibits $Y$ as a closed subscheme of a projective space; hence $Y\to S$ is projective [def-kun-projective], proper [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The graph $V\to V\times_S Y$ of $(J_g)_{g\ne1}$ is the base change of the closed diagonal of $Y$, so is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Write $j$ as a closed immersion into an open $U\subset P$. Base change gives a closed immersion $V\times_S Y\to U\times_S Y$. Composing these two closed immersions [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], then the open immersion $U\times_S Y\to P\times_S Y$, gives precisely $J$.

source.place: Tag 01WD, lemma-segre-embedding; graph as pullback of separated diagonal and base change of the given locally closed immersion

proof.text: Let $a_h$ act on $X$ by $(a_hx)_g=x_{h^{-1}g}$. Then $a_ha_k=a_{hk}$ and $J_g(hv)=j(g^{-1}hv)=(a_hJ(v))_g$, so $J$ is equivariant. Put $E=\{0,\ldots,n\}^H$ and $N=|E|-1=(n+1)^{|H|}-1\geq0$. The iterated Segre map $s:X\to\mathbf P^N_S$ is a closed immersion by [lem-chow-segre]; its coordinates [def-chow-segre] are $z_e=\prod_g x_{g,e(g)}$. Define $b_h$ on projective space by $b_h^*(z_e)=z_{e\circ L_h}$, where $L_h(g)=hg$. Substitution gives $z_e(a_hx)=\prod_gx_{h^{-1}g,e(g)}=\prod_kx_{k,e(hk)}$, hence $s a_h=b_hs$ as scheme morphisms (these are identities of the multihomogeneous coordinate sections). The permutations give $b_hb_k=b_{hk}$. The composite $f=sJ$ is therefore an equivariant immersion: composing the closed part of $J$ with the base change of $s$ and using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] gives a closed immersion into an open of the target, namely the complement of the closed image of $X\setminus U_X$, where $U_X$ is an open through which $J$ factors as closed.

source.place: Tag 01WD, lemma-segre-embedding, coordinate formula; elementary permutation-equivariance computation

proof.text: Apply [lem-chow-closed-model] to the quasi-compact immersion $f:V\to\mathbf P^N_S$ over the affine base $S$. Its scheme-theoretic closure $M\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ contains $V$ as a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme. Its ideal on every affine open $W$ is the kernel of $\mathcal O(W)\to\mathcal O(f^{-1}W)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel]. Equivariance of $f$ identifies this kernel with the kernel on $b_h(W)$: pullback by $b_h$ on the ambient functions and by $h$ on the source gives a commutative square of restriction maps with both vertical maps invertible. Thus $b_h$ preserves the ideal sheaf of $M$, not merely its underlying set, and restricts to an automorphism of $M$. The restrictions satisfy the group law and make $V\hookrightarrow M$ equivariant.

source.place: Tags 01RG (lemma-quasi-compact-immersion) and 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image); kernel invariance is the displayed equivariance square

proof.text: Set $B=R[z_e\mid e\in E]$. Use [lem-per-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal] on the closed subscheme $M\subseteq\mathbf P^N_S$: take its specified ideal $I=\bigoplus I_d$ of homogeneous polynomials whose chart functions vanish on $M$. That statement identifies the canonical closed immersion $\operatorname{Proj}(B/I)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ with $M\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$. Thus the homogeneous presentation is a presentation of the actual scheme-theoretic closure, including all nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, canonical ideal and equality as closed subschemes

proof.text: On $B$ define $\rho_h(z_e)=z_{e\circ L_{h^{-1}}}$ and let $\rho_h$ fix $R$. These graded automorphisms satisfy $\rho_h\rho_k=\rho_{hk}$ by substitution on generators; geometrically $\rho_h=b_{h^{-1}}^*$. For $F\in I_d$ and any $e\in E$, the chart function $\rho_h(F)/z_{e\circ L_{h^{-1}}}^{d}$ is the pullback by $b_{h^{-1}}$ of $F/z_e^d$. Since $b_{h^{-1}}$ preserves $M$ as a closed subscheme by Step 4, this pulled-back function vanishes on $M$ on the corresponding chart. The coordinate permutation runs through all charts. Hence $\rho_h(I_d)\subseteq I_d$ by the chart criterion of [lem-per-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal]; applying $h^{-1}$ gives equality. Therefore $I$ is stable under every $\rho_h$.

source.place: Tag 03GL, chart form of its kernel definition; explicit pullback calculation under coordinate permutations

proof.text: Put $A=B/I$. Stability gives the graded $R$-algebra automorphism $\overline\rho_h([F])=[\rho_h(F)]$, with inverse $\overline\rho_{h^{-1}}$; the group law follows on representatives. By [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] a graded algebra equivalence induces an isomorphism of Proj. Use the usual left-action convention: $h$ acts on $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ by the morphism whose pullback is $\overline\rho_{h^{-1}}$. It is the restriction of $b_h$: on a standard chart the map on coordinate fractions is $[F]/[z_e]^d\mapsto[\rho_{h^{-1}}(F)]/[\rho_{h^{-1}}(z_e)]^d$, the same coordinate substitution as on the ambient projective space. These formulas agree on overlaps because restriction is localization [def-pc-proj]. Thus the identification of Step 5 is equivariant as a scheme identification, and Step 4 gives the required equivariant open immersion into $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$.

source.place: Tag 03GL and the cited Proj equivalence statement; verification on degree-zero localization charts

proof.text: Finally, since $I$ is homogeneous and $B_0=R$, one has $A_0=R/I_0$; the degree-zero map $R\to A_0$ is surjective. The closed immersion from Step 5 makes $M$ projective in [def-kun-projective]. Enumerate the nonempty finite set $E$ to relabel the variables by $z_0,\ldots,z_N$. If $V$ is empty, its kernel ideal sheaf is the unit ideal, $M$ is empty, the canonical homogeneous ideal of Step 5 is all of $B$, and $A=0$ has empty Proj. The same argument also permits $R=0$. No step divided by $|H|$ or used faithfulness; the construction therefore applies to nonfaithful actions and to characteristics dividing $|H|$.

source.place: Tag 03GL; degree-zero quotient calculation and empty case

proof_origin.place: Combination of Tag 01WD, Tag 03GL, and morphisms.tex Tags 01RG and 01R8; equivariance calculated explicitly, not claimed as a verbatim theorem of these sources.
